notes:
User enjoys TV—especially Netflix—and movies centered on history, period settings, biography, social justice, and human rights. They binge-watch and maintain a growing to-watch list, now about 25 titles, which is becoming difficult to organize. They prefer recommendations with meaningful subject matter, strong performances, emotional impact, and historically important or disturbing events.

TV preferences:
- Horror with psychological tension, atmosphere, character development, and plot progression rather than jump scares.
- Complex, cerebral, atmospheric shows, with a good balance of character development and plot advancement.
- Historical dramas similar to “The Crown,” emphasizing strong period settings, royal intrigue, political complexity, romance, and personal relationships.
- Sci-fi involving mystery and supernatural elements, sometimes comparable to “Stranger Things,” but not overly slow or abstract.
- Character-focused historical/social dramas about ordinary or non-royal people living through major events.

Viewing plans and likely watchlist interests:
- Wants to start “Victoria,” a lavish British royal drama about Queen Victoria, Prince Albert, their relationship, and political challenges.
- Was also considering “The Last Kingdom,” an action-oriented historical adventure about Uhtred, Anglo-Saxon/Viking conflict, politics, and battles.
- Chose “The Haunting of Hill House” to try first among horror shows, fitting it around other viewing at roughly 1–2 episodes weekly; attracted by its emphasis on story and characters over jump scares.
- May watch “The OA” later; likes complexity and atmosphere but wants a balance of character and plot and recognizes it is slow-burning.
- Other historical recommendations previously mentioned or potentially saved:
  - Series/miniseries: “Downton Abbey,” “The White Queen,” “Wolf Hall,” “The Tudors,” “Elizabeth I,” “The Spanish Princess,” “Versailles,” “Poldark,” “Outlander,” “Medici: Masters of Florence.”
  - Social-justice-oriented series: “Roots” (2016), “The Underground Railroad,” “When They See Us,” “The Good Fight,” and “The Americans.”
- User was especially interested in the ordinary-person perspective in “Schindler’s List” and “12 Years a Slave.”
- Added “Amistad” and “Hotel Rwanda” to the to-watch list and expects them to be powerful and important.
- Wants more movies or series involving slavery, racism, genocide, war, political repression, LGBTQ+ rights, labor/social movements, and other social-justice or human-rights struggles.
- Relevant movie recommendations include “Schindler’s List,” “12 Years a Slave,” “Hotel Rwanda,” “Amistad,” “Glory,” “The Color Purple,” “Milk,” “Selma,” “The Killing Fields,” “Dead Man Walking,” “Defiance,” and “The Way Back.” Some recommendations center on major public figures rather than ordinary people, so individual titles may be less aligned.
- General royal/period movie recommendations previously given: “The King’s Speech,” “The Young Victoria,” “Elizabeth,” “Shakespeare in Love,” “Atonement,” “The Duchess,” “The New World,” “The Other Boleyn Girl,” “Marie Antoinette,” “Gosford Park,” “The Remains of the Day,” and “The Duellists.”

Documentary interests:
- Wants to learn more about social justice and human rights and stay informed about current issues.
- Documentaries recommended: “The Act of Killing,” “The Cove,” “Super Size Me,” “The Invisible War,” “The Square,” “Blackfish,” “The Look of Silence,” “Citizenfour,” “The Hunting Ground,” and “13th.”
- These cover genocide, surveillance, racial inequality and mass incarceration, sexual assault, political protest, environmental and animal rights, public health, and corporate accountability. User said they will check some out.

Current request/task:
- User wants help organizing the 25-title watchlist because it is becoming hard to track.
- Suggested structure:
  - Historical Dramas
  - Social Justice and Human Rights
  - Royal Dramas
  - Period Pieces
  - Biographical Dramas
  - Documentaries
  - Other
- Possible subcategories under Historical Dramas: World War II, Ancient Civilizations, American History, and European History.
- A practical next step is to ask the user to provide all 25 titles, then sort them into categories, flag duplicates/overlap, and recommend a viewing order. Prioritization could be based on genre/theme, urgency or relevance, ratings, or a balanced mix of fiction and documentaries.
